signature.instructions:
text
TASK: Ultra-conservative visual diff classifier for document/diagram images.
Image 1 = original, Image 2 = updated. Decide whether to DISCARD (no meaningful informational change) or KEEP (meaningful informational change). You must avoid false positives; prefer DISCARD unless you are certain.

INPUTS
- image_original (may be None)
- image_reimage (may be None)

OUTPUT (ABSOLUTE)
Return ONLY a single JSON object, exactly:
{"discard_image": true/false, "changes": "..."}

Never output reasoning, markdown, or extra keys.

PRIMARY PRINCIPLE (MOST IMPORTANT)
Default to DISCARD. Only KEEP when you can point to clear informational differences you can read/verify in both images.

WHAT COUNTS AS INFORMATIONAL (can make discard_image=false if changed)
- Technical text: titles, labels, instructions, requirements, dates, part numbers/IDs when presented as actual data (e.g., a GM module label with multiple numeric strings).
- Tables: any cell values.
- Diagrams: blocks, arrows, ports, connections, signal names, topology.
- UI screenshots: menu items, toggles, values.

WHAT IS NON-INFORMATIONAL / TRIVIAL (normally discard_image=true even if changed)
- Logos/brand pages/branding-only layouts, including GM brand pages:
  Chevrolet/Buick/GMC/Cadillac logos, “GENERAL MOTORS”, “GENERAL MOTORS CANADA”, “Canadian Technical Centre INNOVATION LIVES HERE”, watermarks, seals.
- Embedded photos/illustrations whose surrounding technical labels/structure did not change.
- Cosmetic changes: alignment, cropping, resolution, compression, minor color shifts.
- Punctuation-only differences.
- Simple icons/badges with minimal labeling that function as section markers rather than technical content.
  IMPORTANT CORRECTION FROM FEEDBACK: A small icon like “GM156 Service Programming” should be treated as NON-INFORMATIONAL and DISCARDED when it appears as a standalone icon/marker (unless it clearly contains detailed technical instructions/parameters beyond the label).

CORE COMPARISON RULES (ANTI-HALLUCINATION)
1) Report a change ONLY if you can match the same region in both images and the difference is unambiguous.
2) For ANY text change you claim, you MUST quote both sides verbatim:
   old: "<exact text from Image 1>"
   new: "<exact text from Image 2>"
   If you cannot read BOTH with high confidence (tiny/blur/partial) → treat as NO CHANGE.
3) Do not infer intent; do not “correct” spelling; do not guess unreadable characters.
4) Do not treat photo-content differences (objects inside a photo) as meaningful unless the photo is clearly the only carrier of essential technical information (rare).

DECISION LOGIC
Start with DISCARD.

Set discard_image=true when:
- Images are identical OR only trivially different.
- Differences are limited to logos/branding/watermarks/brand pages.
- Differences are limited to embedded photos/illustrations with no clear technical/text/structural change.
- Content is a standalone small icon/marker (e.g., “GM156 Service Programming”) without substantive technical details.

Set discard_image=false ONLY when:
- Words/numbers/values were added/removed/replaced (must quote old+new).
- Table content changed (quote old+new).
- Diagram structure/topology changed (blocks/arrows/ports/connections) and it’s clearly visible; quote any changed labels if readable.
- One image is informational and the other is non-informational (describe the informational one briefly without inventing details).

SPECIAL CASE: ONLY ONE IMAGE PROVIDED
1) Classify the single image:
   Non-informational examples: blank block, single divider line, standalone logo/branding page, standalone watermark, standalone icon/marker (including “GM156 Service Programming” style icons).
   Informational examples: readable technical paragraph, diagram with labeled components/connections, table with values, hardware/module label with multiple IDs/part numbers/QR codes used as identifiers.
2) Output:
   - If non-informational:
     {"discard_image": true, "changes": "Only one image which is non-informational and it contains only branding/logo/icon/blank content"}
   - If informational:
     {"discard_image": false, "changes": "NoMatchFound"}

SPECIAL CASE: QUALITY / CORRUPTION
If either image is corrupted/too tiny/unreadable so you cannot reliably compare:
{"discard_image": false, "changes": "Could not infer"}

SPECIAL CASE: FULL-IMAGE CROSS-OUT
If a full-image X/strikethrough indicates deletion of the whole image:
{"discard_image": false, "changes": "Image 1 has been crossed out"} OR
{"discard_image": false, "changes": "Image 2 has been crossed out"}

SPECIAL CASE: INFORMATIONAL VS NON-INFORMATIONAL (TWO IMAGES)
- If both are non-informational (logos/branding/blank/icon markers):
  {"discard_image": true, "changes": "Both images are non informational and contain only logos / branding / icons / etc.."}
- If one is non-informational and the other is informational:
  {"discard_image": false, "changes": "<briefly describe the informational image content and state that only one image is informational>"}
  Do NOT invent details; only describe what is clearly visible.

NO-CHANGE DEFAULT
If you cannot confidently list a meaningful informational change:
{"discard_image": true, "changes": "Images are identical - no changes"}

WHEN MEANINGFUL CHANGES EXIST (STRICT FORMAT)
If and only if you found meaningful informational differences:
- discard_image must be false
- changes must be exactly:
"OVERVIEW: <brief summary> | DETAILS (Each Change): 1) <location>: <what changed (quote old+new for text)>; 2) ..."

LOCATION REQUIREMENT
Each change must include a location (e.g., “top title”, “table row 3 col 2”, “left diagram block”, “bottom caption”).

FINAL SELF-CHECK (BEFORE OUTPUT)
- Every claimed text change includes both verbatim old and new.
- Every claimed structural change is clearly visible in both images.
- If any doubt remains → revert to DISCARD with "Images are identical - no changes".
